format: Text with inline TeX in $...$ and display TeX in $$...$$. Glossary symbol and units fields are TeX without delimiters.

terms.definition: A vector of length one that only gives a direction: $\hat{\mathbf{a}}=\mathbf{A}/|\mathbf{A}|$.
The vector from the origin to a point: $\mathbf{R}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}x+\hat{\mathbf{y}}y+\hat{\mathbf{z}}z$.
The vector from point 1 to point 2: $\mathbf{R}_{12}=\mathbf{R}_2-\mathbf{R}_1$. Used constantly in Coulomb's law and Biot–Savart.
$|\mathbf{A}||\mathbf{B}|\cos\theta$, a scalar. It picks out the component of one vector along another.
A vector perpendicular to both, of length $|\mathbf{A}||\mathbf{B}|\sin\theta$, direction by the right-hand rule. Note $\mathbf{B}\times\mathbf{A}=-\mathbf{A}\times\mathbf{B}$.
Three perpendicular axes with unit vectors $\hat{\mathbf{x}},\hat{\mathbf{y}},\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ that point the same way everywhere.
Radial distance $r$ from the $z$-axis, azimuth $\phi$ from the $+x$ axis, and height $z$. Natural for wires, coax and solenoids.
Distance $R$ from the origin, polar angle $\theta$ down from $+z$, and azimuth $\phi$. Natural for point charges and spheres.
A tiny step along a path. Its components carry the scale factors: $r\,d\phi$ in cylindrical, $R\,d\theta$ and $R\sin\theta\,d\phi$ in spherical.
A tiny patch of surface, pointing along its normal. On a closed surface the normal points outward.
Adds up the component of $\mathbf{A}$ along a path. For a force it is the work done; around a closed loop it is the circulation.
How much of a vector field passes through a surface.
A vector pointing toward the fastest increase of a scalar field, with magnitude equal to that rate of increase.
Net outward flux per unit volume at a point: positive at sources, negative at sinks.
Circulation per unit area at a point, pointing along the axis a tiny paddle wheel would spin around.
Turns a volume integral of divergence into a flux through the closed surface: $\int_V\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}\,dV=\oint_S\mathbf{A}\cdot d\mathbf{s}$.
Turns a surface integral of curl into a line integral around the boundary: $\int_S(\nabla\times\mathbf{A})\cdot d\mathbf{s}=\oint_C\mathbf{A}\cdot d\mathbf{l}$.
The divergence of the gradient. $\nabla^2V=0$ (Laplace's equation) holds wherever there is no charge.
A field with zero divergence everywhere, so its field lines have no beginning or end. $\mathbf{B}$ is always solenoidal.
A field with zero curl, so it is the gradient of a scalar and its line integrals do not depend on the path. Static $\mathbf{E}$ is conservative.
